content:
Sean Gallagher: We need to lock default metric gates for canary apply (Optimize config changes) before we merge canary support. Asking for proposed thresholds per tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) + what signals are hard fail vs warn. Goal: stop “bad batching/quant” from nuking p95 + errors. 

Aisha Bello: Draft proposal based on existing SLO/error budget + what we can reliably measure in 5–10m canary windows. Assumptions: canary 5% traffic (Hosted) or 1 shard (Dedicated/Private), evaluation window 10m, baseline window 30m trailing (same day). 

Aisha Bello: Hard fail signals (abort rollout):
- `p95_latency_ms` regression > +15% AND > +30ms absolute (whichever is larger)
- `http_5xx_rate` > 0.3% OR > 2x baseline (baseline min floor 0.05%)
- `inference_timeout_rate` > 0.1% OR > 2x baseline
- `gpu_saturation` (see below) sustained > 90% for 5m (to catch “queueing death spiral”)

Aisha Bello: Warn-only (continue but flag + require manual ack to proceed past 25%):
- `p50_latency_ms` > +10%
- `p99_latency_ms` > +20% (p99 noisy; better as warning)
- `token_throughput_per_gpu` drop > 10% (if we can compute confidently for that model)

Allison Grant: +1 on absolute floor + relative delta. Otherwise we’ll false fail during low traffic. For saturation, can we define the actual metric? We’ve got `gpu_utilization` and `scheduler_queue_depth`—util alone is misleading.

Caleb Johnson: For “saturation” I’d gate on a composite we already have in telemetry (used for capacity alerts):
- `scheduler_queue_depth_p95` (per shard) and `scheduler_wait_ms_p95`
If either blows up, user-facing latency follows.

Logan Wright: Agree. GPU util is high even when healthy. Better: queue wait + active requests. Proposed hard-fail saturation gate:
- `scheduler_wait_ms_p95` > 2x baseline AND > 15ms absolute for 3/5 minutes
- OR `scheduler_queue_depth_p95` > 2x baseline AND > 50 absolute for 3/5 minutes

Rafael Mendes: From on-call POV: prefer fewer gates but ones that correlate with “users are mad.” p95 latency + timeout + 5xx are the big 3. Queue wait is good if it’s stable.

Paula Mendes: Product asks: can we have different thresholds per tier? Enterprise Dedicated wants more conservative gates (they’d rather abort than risk). Hosted sandbox can be looser.

Neha Kapoor: Yep. Let’s define tiers explicitly:
- Tier A: internal/staging
- Tier B: Hosted prod (shared)
- Tier C: Dedicated/Private prod (single tenant)
Need defaults + override policy (who can override, and do we require a justification string + ticket link).

Jada Williams: Implementation detail: the gate engine can take per-scope policy. We can ship a default policy matrix + allow per-tenant override behind RBAC.

Dylan Brooks: Console copy needs to reflect “this is a safety check, not a perf guarantee.” But we should show the exact thresholds in the canary step.

Aisha Bello: Updating with tier-specific:

Aisha Bello: Tier A (internal/staging) — avoid flakiness
- Hard fail:
  - p95 latency: +25% AND +50ms
  - 5xx: >0.5% OR >3x baseline
  - timeouts: >0.2% OR >3x baseline
  - saturation: scheduler_wait_ms_p95 > 3x baseline AND > 25ms
- Warn:
  - p99 +30%

Aisha Bello: Tier B (Hosted prod)
- Hard fail:
  - p95 latency: +15% AND +30ms
  - 5xx: >0.3% OR >2x baseline
  - timeouts: >0.1% OR >2x baseline
  - saturation: scheduler_wait_ms_p95 > 2x baseline AND > 15ms (3/5m)
- Warn:
  - p99 +20%
  - p50 +10%

Aisha Bello: Tier C (Dedicated/Private prod) — conservative
- Hard fail:
  - p95 latency: +10% AND +20ms
  - 5xx: >0.2% OR >2x baseline
  - timeouts: >0.05% OR >2x baseline
  - saturation: scheduler_wait_ms_p95 > 1.5x baseline AND > 10ms (3/5m)
- Warn:
  - p99 +15%

Allison Grant: For 5xx and timeouts, we should clarify it’s request-level, not token-level errors. Also: do we include “model server oom/restart rate”?

Caleb Johnson: We can gate on `runtime_restart_count` but it’s too sparse for 10m windows unless it’s catastrophic. Maybe add as hard fail if >0 in canary window (for Tier C?)

Rafael Mendes: If a canary causes a restart, I want it to abort immediately. That’s exactly what we’re trying to prevent.

Neha Kapoor: Agreed: add a “catastrophic” gate across all tiers:
- If `model_server_restarts` >= 1 during canary window => hard fail
Also add `config_apply_errors` (control plane/runtime propagation) as separate “apply health” gate.

incident-bot: (FYI) Similar to INC-2147 pattern: latency spike + queue wait + eventual restarts. Linking runbook section draft: https://confluence.redwoodinference.example/eng-sre/runbooks/rollback-optimize-config-in-production#metric-gates

Sean Gallagher: Good. Let’s also define baseline logic so we don’t argue later.
- Use trailing 30m baseline (excluding last 2m to avoid overlap), min sample size: 500 requests OR 50k tokens. If below, fall back to absolute thresholds only and treat deltas as warn.
- Gate evaluation: 10m canary, compute per-minute, require breach in 3 of last 5 minutes (except catastrophic gates).

Logan Wright: +1. In code we can implement “burn rate” style checks too, but maybe phase 2. Keep it simple.

Paula Mendes: Can we add cost/throughput gates? Like if throughput drops a ton we’re hurting unit economics.

Aisha Bello: Cost gates are tricky in 10m; metering lag. I’d keep “throughput per GPU” as warn-only for now; we can surface it in the UI.

Dylan Brooks: UI-wise: we can show:
- Current value vs baseline
- Threshold
- Status (pass/warn/fail)
And an “Override + proceed” button only for warn states (not fail). For override we’ll require a ticket link.

Allison Grant: Override policy should be RBAC: only `optimize.config.apply.override_gates` (or similar) for Tier C. Everyone else can only abort/rollback.

Jada Williams: Noted. We already have `optimize.config.apply` and `optimize.config.rollback`. We can add an override permission or treat “override” as separate endpoint requiring elevated role.

Sean Gallagher: Decision summary (unless objections by EOD):
1) Ship gate matrix as Aisha posted (Tier A/B/C) with saturation defined on `scheduler_wait_ms_p95` (and optionally queue depth as supporting signal, not a hard requirement).
2) Add catastrophic hard fail across all tiers: any model server restart in canary window.
3) Baseline: 30m trailing + min sample logic; if low sample, use absolute thresholds only.
4) Warns require manual ack; fails abort canary apply automatically.
5) Overrides: gated by RBAC + requires justification + ticket link; log to audit events.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: Works for on-call.

Neha Kapoor: :thumbsup: Please make sure dashboards have a single “Canary Gate Health” panel we can screenshot during incidents.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: Also ensure correlation id (apply_id) is propagated into metrics tags so we can pivot.

Caleb Johnson: I’ll add `apply_id` tag to the gate evaluation events + link to traces where available.

Sean Gallagher: Cool. Aisha/Logan/Caleb please drop this into the thresholds sheet + ping Dylan for Console strings. I’ll update the runbook section with the final defaults.
